business_scenario:
A store manager wants to compare activity across categories. The team has records of customers, orders and order items.

For every order, show its number and separate totals of order-item amount for order items marked Completed, Pending and Failed. Other statuses contribute to none of these totals. Show zero for a status with no order items. Arrange the list by order number, smallest first.

How would you prepare this information? Explain your approach in your own words. You do not need to write SQL.
solution_approach: I will join orders and order items to conditionally sum Completed, Pending and Failed event amounts per orders.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); orders(order_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, order_date, status, order_total); order_items(order_item_id PK, order_id FK, item_date, item_type, quantity, amount, status)
learner_question: Should every order display Completed, Pending, and Failed totals even when some are zero?
manager_reply: Yes. Show all three status totals for every order, using zero whenever no matching order items exist.

business_scenario:
A store manager wants to prepare an up-to-date review. The team has records of customers, orders and order items.

For each order with order items, select the one with the latest date. If several share that date, select the largest order item number. Show its order item number, order number, date, type, order-item amount and status. Include all activity statuses and omit orders without activity. Arrange the list by order number, smallest first.

How would you prepare this information? Explain your approach in your own words. You do not need to write SQL.
solution_approach: I will row number order items partitioned by order id from newest to oldest by item date and order item id. I will keep row number 1 as the latest event.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); orders(order_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, order_date, status, order_total); order_items(order_item_id PK, order_id FK, item_date, item_type, quantity, amount, status)
learner_question: If an order has multiple order items on its latest item date, which one should be selected?
manager_reply: Pick the order item with the largest order item number on that latest date, and omit orders without order items.
